tilts.set: SET on 2026-11-06 by the Portfolio Fitness for Fighting judg

industry.why: Double Underweight, carried unchanged, with the counter-case strengthened and named. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): property is valued off a yield and financed with leverage, the US 10-year is near 5.10%, the Fed hikes in December, and real estate was not spoken to as an industry. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: F now, D prior at industry level, every property sector D or F. The counter-case is stronger this week than at any time since the row was set: yields fell on firm data, Goldman Sachs upgraded bonds to overweight 'moving from headwind to hedge' (16 and 19 Oct), and real estate investment trusts were among the only sectors bought (Jefferies desk, 17 Oct); if that rally is a trend, this is the row where the tilt costs most, and it is the first row I would lift. Held at F because one week's rally with the policy rate still rising is a hedge working, not a peak, and the condition on the sector rows (back to D if the US 10-year falls under 4.5%) is 60 basis points away.

sector.key: N.2. Real estate - commercial landlords (offices and diversified)
sector.why: Double Underweight, set deliberately this week (carried F from the old TBD property row), matching its industry. Component 1 regime, 16-Oct-26 (a discount-rate shock with the first credit crack inside the artificial intelligence chain: United States core inflation re-accelerating on energy, the Fed and Bank of England hikes pulled forward, the US 10-year about 5.1%, the US joined the sell-off and Asia is in washout, defensives bid for four weeks in Europe, European breadth off its three-year lows but in the bottom quarter, the consumer forecast to weaken into winter; sources present 2026-W42): property is valued off a yield and leveraged, so the discount-rate line lands directly and twice (asset values and refinancing), and this week Norway's Entra posted a large valuation loss while Goldman Sachs tied each 100 basis points of rates to a 6% fall in housing investment. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-16 against 2026-08-14, not week on week: F now, F prior. The 38 stocks are the universe's largest property group and none is in the MI Pool. Counter-case: British Land beat with 3 to 5% rental growth guidance (Outset Global, 15-Oct), GOAL's barbell wants bond proxies, and this is the row where a rates-relief rally costs most; back to D if the US 10-year falls under 4.5%.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No source spoke to Spain this week (a source pack is present, 2026-W43, and it carried nothing country-specific here), relative strength is not graded by country, and Richard's view is G10 and Europe-wide with no country line. An absence is an absence; no tilt.
